title: The iPhone's Web-Only Launch and the Birth of the App Store (2007-2008)
explainer: When the original iPhone shipped in June 2007, Apple deliberately blocked third-party native apps and told developers to build 'Web 2.0' applications that ran entirely inside Safari, arguing this preserved security and stability. Only a year later, after sustained developer pressure, did Apple reverse course and release a native SDK alongside the App Store in July 2008. The native-vs-web split this lesson teaches isn't a law of nature - it's the direct legacy of a platform owner's policy decision that was itself reversed within twelve months.

title: Electron and the Rise of Web-Powered Desktop Apps (2013)
explainer: Electron began in 2013 as 'Atom Shell,' built by GitHub engineers specifically to power their new Atom text editor by fusing a Node.js runtime with the Chromium browser engine inside one desktop process. Its success - quickly adopted for Slack, Visual Studio Code, and many others - is the concrete historical reason 'cross-platform desktop apps built from web technology' became a standard, named category of software rather than a one-off hack.
